findings.title: Index-staleness: theoretically possible but unexercisable in practice
findings.detail: onPanelStepSubmit reads sel.stepIndex which was captured in selectedNode at click time (selectNode call). If another step is deleted WHILE the side panel is open (shifting array indices), sel.stepIndex could point at the wrong record. Assessment: NOT a real risk in the current flow. The delete flow goes through requestDelete → confirmDelete on the canvas itself. confirmDelete at line 383 explicitly calls clearSelection() when the deleted node was the selected one. More importantly, deleting a DIFFERENT step (not the open one) would emit update:steps to the page, which would re-render FunnelCanvas with new props.steps — but selectedNode is internal canvas state and does NOT get reset by a props change. This is the one genuine staleness path: (1) open step A at index 0, (2) delete step B at index 0 which shifts A to a new index, (3) confirm save — sel.stepIndex=0 now points at the wrong step. However: the guard `!(props.steps ?? [])[idx]` only checks that the slot is non-empty, not that it still contains the intended step. The slot would be non-empty (shifted A is now there), so the overwrite would corrupt A with B's form state. This is a real logical gap but extremely low-probability in the single-user editor context (requires deleting a different node while the panel is open on another, then immediately submitting the open panel). Non-blocking for this fix; worth a follow-up guard (e.g. also validate that props.steps[idx].id matches sel.step.id when both are non-null).
findings.recommendation: Follow-up: add an id-consistency cross-check as a secondary guard in onPanelStepSubmit: after the index check, if both sel.step?.id and props.steps[idx]?.id are non-null and they differ, bail (return). This covers the shift-by-delete race without breaking the null-id fresh-node path that this fix targets.

findings.title: onCanvasStepSave checks steps AFTER update:steps has already fired, which is correct — but relies on emit ordering
findings.detail: The canvas always emits update:steps before step-save (line 300-301 in FunnelCanvas.client.vue). The page handles update:steps via onCanvasSteps which mutates steps.value synchronously, then calls persistSteps(). onCanvasStepSave then runs against the already-updated steps.value — so the readiness check in onCanvasStepSave sees the committed (new) step content, not the stale seed. This ordering is load-bearing and correct as implemented. Vue event handlers execute synchronously in order, so this is stable.
findings.recommendation: No code change needed. Consider a brief comment in onCanvasStepSave noting the dependency on update:steps firing first (already handled by onCanvasSteps above it in the template binding order).

summary: The fix is correct and robust. The core change — routing side-panel step edits by array index instead of id — correctly addresses the silent no-op bug for id:null (freshly-added) nodes, and the index-guard chain (kind==='step' + stepIndex!=null + Number.isInteger + slot-exists) is solid. One theoretical staleness scenario exists: selecting step A at index N, then deleting a different step that shifts A's index, then submitting the panel — the index guard would not catch this because the slot is non-empty (it now contains A shifted). This is a non-blocking follow-up (the comment in F1 recommends adding an id-consistency cross-check). All other checks — explicit Save feedback, PATCH count, implicit autosave gate, i18n parity, no prop mutation, test coverage across 6 scenarios — pass cleanly. Verdict: PASS, 0 blockers, 2 minor informational findings.
